utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-74-A, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to begin by checking that the audio equipment is working properly. Can the appellants hear the proceedings in a language that they understand? Let me start with Mr. Prlic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I hear you and I understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Prlic. Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT STOJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Everything is all right, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojic. Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is all right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Praljak. Mr. Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PETKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everything is fine. I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everything is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINZAUTI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we hear you. And for the record, it's Giulia Pinzauti, Senior Appeals Counsel Douglas Stringer, and Case Manager Colin Nawrot appearing for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I note that on September 15th Mr. Pusic filed his consent to hold today's Status Conference in his absence. Appearances for the Prosecution in fact we already have had, so appearances for the Defence. For Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Michael Karnavas for Dr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. For Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Senka Nozica. Together with me in the courtroom is Molly Martin, pro bono legal assistant, for the Defence of Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Nozica. For Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Nika Pinter for General Praljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pinter. For Mr. Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. For General Petkovic, Vesna Alaburic, Defence Attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Alaburic. For Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: MR. PLAVEC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, good afternoon. Drazen Plavec, co-counsel for Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Plavec. And for Mr. Pusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. For Mr. Pusic, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic attorney from Sarajevo. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ibrisimovic. As you are all aware, the Rule 65 bis B of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the last Status Conference has been held for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. The Status Conference serves two primary purposes. First, it allows the appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions and for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained persons. Second it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. In the present case, the last Status Conference was held on 27 May 2014. Today's Status Conference was scheduled by order filed on 2 September 2014. I now turn to discuss situation of health of the appellants and I would at the same time inquire into detention conditions. And if any one of you wishes, I could close the session and have a private one. Let me start -- we will do it seriatim. Mr. Prlic, do you have any matters that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRLIC
utterances.text: I'm fine so far, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I hope you will be fine in the future, too.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRLIC
utterances.text: It depends on you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Prlic. We now turn to Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT STOJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everything is fine, no problems so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, same comment which I made to Mr. Prlic. I hope that this will apply to the future as well. Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no problems, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Praljak. Mr. Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PETKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no problems at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have some small issues but not so important that they would necessitate me to talk about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Up to you. Now I am here to be -- to listen to whatever you'd like to say especially about health and conditions of detention. But you know best and I am glad that you don't appear to have anything which is of great importance now. So I will now turn to recent procedural history. Update on the case. I note that the English translation of the trial judgement was filed on 6 June 2014 and that in accordance with the decision issued on 21 June 2013, Mr. Prlic, Mr. Stojic, Mr. Petkovic, and Mr. Coric filed their Notices of Appeal in early August 2014. All Notices of Appeal have now therefore been filed. I further recall that I ordered Mr. Praljak, Mr. Pusic, and the Prosecution to file their appellant's briefs no later than 135 days from the issuance of the official English translation of the trial judgement so that there was a harmonised briefing schedule in place for all parties. In early August, all Defence teams and the Prosecution filed motions for extensions of the work limit and/or the time limits for the filing of their appellant's briefs. The Prosecution also requested an extension of the time to file its respondent's briefs. I issued the decision on 22 August 2014 granting the relief sought in part. At the end of August and early September, Mr. Coric, who was joined by all of his co-appellants as well as by the Prosecution filed motions for reconsideration of this decision. On 5 September, I issued a decision finding that the reconsideration was warranted but only in relation to the relief that had been requested by the Prosecution for an extension of its deadline to file the respondent's briefs. On 15 September, 2014, Mr. Prlic filed a motion requesting that I refer the requests for extension of time and word limit to the Bench of the Appeals Chamber seized of this case. In the days thereafter, he was joined by Mr. Praljak, Mr. Petkovic, Mr. Coric, and Mr. Stojic. The Prosecution filed a response to Mr. Prlic's request. On 18 September 2014, I issued a decision granting the request for a referral to the panel of Judges. The matter is therefore currently before the Appeals Chamber and a decision will be issued in due course. At this point, I would like to ask you whether you, the parties, either the appellants or the Prosecution have any points that they would like to raise? Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I do have one point to raise and that is on the issue of the level of this particular appeal. It was a level 3 throughout the trial, we had a five-year trial, we waited two years plus for the judgement to come out, we waited another year plus for the translation, we filed our notices on time. Thereafter, we were required to notify the Registrar as to what level we thought the case was. We all have submitted our respective notices that this is a level 3. We have yet to hear from the Registrar, and we understand, perhaps, the Registrar wishes to hear back from the Appeal Chamber itself. Be that as it may, I raise this issue because this is a very, very large appeal. It requires a team, a team requires to be paid. And in order for us to do our level best to meet our professional and ethical obligations, especially with these very tight deadlines, especially if the extension is not granted, it's virtually impossible to do so. It's a Herculean task as it is and I think that Hercules himself would probably buckle under the pressure that all of us are suffering from, so to the extent possible, Mr. President, Your Honour, if you could consult with your colleagues and consult with the Registrar regarding the level of this particular case we would be most grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please. Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINZAUTI
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. No, we have nothing to raise.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Nothing to raise. And since -- I'm terribly sorry, please ...

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was sitting down so it was not easy to see me. Following up on Mr. Karnavas's words and the short deadlines for the preparation of our appeal and in compliance with the wish of my client and all the others, I'd like to say that I would like to participate in the appeals. When can we expect the translation of the judgement into Croatian? We have been informed by the Registrar that would happen in late September but we would be glad to know whether this will happen within the next few days or when? This is very important for our consultations with our clients about finalising our appeals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Regarding the time which the date for the submission of the translation to which you have referred, it is still my expectation that it will come out in September. That's the information which you need now; correct? And I want to --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. If there is nothing more precise than that, then I suppose this is it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, there are not so many days left in September, I think, that if I say it will be in September, it's -- it gives you a pretty good indication.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It may seem like a bit of an exaggeration, but when there is so little time left for drafting an appeal, every day matters. I would like to apologise to you for having been so insistent on more precise information. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: If I would have known exactly the day of September, I can assure you that I would have given it to you. I think that the indication that you have is close enough, I hope, and good enough for you your immediate needs, and I also would like to assure the appellants that we are working expeditiously on their request which was referred to the entire panel regarding the deadlines. I believe that unless there is anything else, this brings us to the end of our Status Conference, and I would like to thank the parties for their attendance and adjourn these proceedings.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
